headline: FDA rejects ivonescimab for EGFR-mutant lung cancer, citing 93% of trial events in China
dek: A complete response letter to Summit Therapeutics says 257 of 275 progressions or deaths in the HARMONi trial occurred in China, and questions the efficacy and safety balance.
body:
The US Food and Drug Administration has rejected ivonescimab, Akeso's bispecific antibody, for advanced non-small cell lung cancer, according to ruibao.news. The decision is set out in a complete response letter dated 13 November to Summit Therapeutics, Akeso's US partner, which filed the application on 14 November 2025.

The FDA's first objection concerned where patients were enrolled. Of 275 cancer progressions or deaths in the HARMONi trial, 257 occurred among patients enrolled in China, and the agency said it could not tell whether the result applied to Americans. HARMONi enrolled 438 patients with EGFR-mutant disease who had stopped responding to EGFR-targeted treatment, and 165 of them came from North America and Europe. Patients received platinum-based chemotherapy plus either ivonescimab or placebo.

The second objection concerned efficacy. Median progression-free survival was 6.8 months on ivonescimab against 4.4 months on chemotherapy alone, a 48% lower risk. Median overall survival was 16.8 months against 14.0 months. That 2.8-month gap missed the statistical threshold set before the trial. The FDA said the share of patients whose tumours shrank did not differ substantially between the groups, reported as 44.7% on the drug and 34.2% on chemotherapy alone.

The letter cites serious immune-related side effects and others linked to blocking VEGF. It says: "The modest improvement in median PFS does not outweigh the risks of ivonescimab as an add-on to chemotherapy."

On 22 July 2026, Summit released longer follow-up showing a roughly 24% lower risk of death on ivonescimab, and said it had shared the figures with the FDA.
key_quote: The modest improvement in median PFS does not outweigh the risks of ivonescimab as an add-on to chemotherapy

source.title: FDA Ivonescimab Letter: 93% of Key Trial Events Were in China
